payload.rationale: The root cause is in camelCase (src/text.js:41): non-first words capitalize the character at index 1 instead of index 0 (`lower[1].toUpperCase() + lower.slice(1)`). This uppercases the second character while slice(1) keeps it in place, leaving the first character lowercase — e.g. 'big' becomes 'Iig' instead of 'Big', producing 'helloIigOorld' instead of 'helloBigWorld'. Changing the index to 0 makes the first character uppercase and slice(1) correctly appends the remaining lowercase characters. This also fixes the TypeError for single-character words, since `lower[1]` would be undefined while `lower[0]` always exists for the non-empty words guaranteed by `.filter(Boolean)`.
